competition.flat_book_pnl: A flat seat has zero net financing/competition P&L: paper NAV earning SOFR is benchmarked at SOFR, so those flows cancel, and shocked-risk financing is zero.
competition.funding_basis: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 is the zero-return competition benchmark, not free alpha. Every seat has $100m paper NAV that may be described as earning SOFR, but that capital is equally funded/benchmarked at SOFR so those flows cancel. Deployed shocked-risk capital pays the same official SOFR on trusted standard-shock risk capital: the absolute MTM loss from a 1% adverse spot move, a 100bp (1 percentage point) adverse outright rate move, or a 100bp adverse curve/RV spread move under the trusted duration-1 P&L convention. Equal risk capital receives equal financing treatment across asset classes. Notional is descriptive, not the funding base. A completely flat book — including no-trade-skeptic — therefore has zero net financing/competition P&L from SOFR cash or funding economics. Positive financing/carry alpha requires an explicit markable strategy that earns above SOFR or funds below SOFR. Weekends and holidays carry the last applicable published fixing until the next fixing. If official fixing history cannot be established, new funding accrual fails closed and prior canonical balances are preserved.
competition.instruction: Do not optimize for gross notional or fill available capacity. Size risk from plausible adverse paths and historical excursions while staying inside the trusted risk-capital and drawdown limits. Flat cash at SOFR is the zero benchmark, not a source of alpha. The no-trade-skeptic must include a structured funding_view on every new risk or NO_TRADE thesis: the frozen official SOFR fixing, the relevant SR3 forward-curve view, its own assessment of whether realized funding will print higher, lower, or about the same as the curve, and the implication for remaining at the zero SOFR benchmark versus paying SOFR on shocked-risk capital.
competition.objective: Finish with the highest cumulative net paper P&L across the 14 standing seats.

causal.original_belief: The US-Canada rate gap would keep winner-size long USDCAD intact through oil and CAD-impulse noise after the material extension.
causal.observed_reality: A material winner then a large giveback, with spot through entry, coincident with three-digit oil, rising Canadian impulse, and a Bank of Canada hike poll to 2.50.
causal.assumptions_right: The dollar still has a clean rate advantage versus CAD, USDCAD is the right dollar-spot expression of that gap, and a leftover rates stub can remain after harvest.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Three-digit oil plus rising Canadian impulse is a harvest catalyst at winner size, not residual noise; the hike poll compresses policy optics on the CAD leg.
causal.causal_divergence: The rate-gap thesis still explains why some dollar-versus-CAD edge exists. It does not explain keeping winner size after the harvest trigger printed. The break is post-extension sizing, not a failed dollar-versus-CAD expression.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: The same frozen tape already implied cutting winner size and, at most, a reduced residual long. Holding 8 million was not implied by the rate gap alone; initiating 8 million from flat on this packet would also have been a no.
causal.future_implication: After a material USDCAD win, three-digit oil plus rising Canadian impulse remains the harvest trigger; leftover US rate edge is expressed in reduced size, not winner size.

postmortems.thesis_assessment: CAD-bull versus the dollar was fine as a macro lean. The claim that spot was a unique fade of crowded long-dollar was not.
postmortems.expression_assessment: Failed. Spot FX was not the unique instrument. The unique remaining expression was the March 2027 pay; USDCAD was the crowded overlay.
postmortems.timing_assessment: The roughly 19-day window captured the 1.42 to 1.41 move and the 21 October close. Timing of the FX trade is not the defect.
postmortems.sizing_assessment: Sizing is not the defect. The error was stacking a second CAD-bull expression rather than the dollars put on the short.
postmortems.lesson: A profitable CAD-bull spot fade is still a bad expression if the desk already owns the same CAD-bull through dove and carry receives and leftover dollar-king positioning. Uniqueness of ownership is the trade, not a restatement of the CAD tape.
postmortems.future_rule: Before adding spot FX as a crowded-dollar fade or CAD-bull, list existing rates and leftover FX ownership. If the new trade is the same CAD-bull overlay, skip spot and hold the existing rates pay. Do not mint a March 2027 CORRA receive to balance a closed FX short.

causal.original_belief: Short USDCAD was a unique fade of a crowded long-dollar book, cleaner than adding another dollar short, and distinct from rates CAD-bull already owned.
causal.observed_reality: USDCAD fell from 1.42 to 1.41 over about 19 days and was closed on 21 October, after which the desk paid CORRA March 2027. Direction paid. Ownership was not unique: carry and dove receives plus leftover dollar-king long already supplied CAD-bull.
causal.assumptions_right: CAD outperformed the dollar over the holding window. Closing the FX short and expressing the residual view in the March 2027 pay moved risk toward the rates path.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Uniqueness of ownership. The pitch treated a CAD-bull spot short as a distinct crowded-dollar fade rather than a duplicate overlay on dove/carry receives and leftover dollar-king CAD.
causal.causal_divergence: The gap is ownership uniqueness, not whether CAD-bull was confirmed. Short USDCAD did not uniquely fade crowded long-dollar; it stacked the same CAD-bull the desk already owned. The later March 2027 pay is the tell that the distinct expression was the rates path and spot was the second overlay.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: On the same information — crowded long-dollar narrative plus CAD-bull already owned in dove/carry receives and dollar-king leftover — a uniqueness check would have rejected short USDCAD and kept risk in a CORRA pay or in flat FX.
causal.future_implication: Do not re-short USDCAD as a crowded-dollar fade while dove/carry CAD-bull remains on. Hold the existing March 2027 pay. Do not add a March 2027 receive as a balance to the closed FX short.

vol-convexity.thesis: The book is already flat, so there is no residual delta that a vol overlay needs to bound, and VIX at 19.03 is a headline print rather than a tradeable surface. Spot remains the wrong default when timing is uncertain or event risk is underpriced, but this frozen packet has no option-chain marks, strikes, or implieds, so a risk-reversal, fly, or other bounded-risk structure cannot be specified without inventing prices. Until a marked chain is in the packet, the only honest expression in this remit is none.

no-trade-skeptic.thesis: Apparent edges in this packet are already in the SOFR strip, too noisy versus an overnight horizon, and poorly timed against a book that is already flat. Official NY Fed SOFR is 3.90 percent ACT/360 dated 22 October; the same packet prices December 2026 4.17, March 2027 4.37, June 2027 4.51 and September 2027 4.56. That upward path is the market, not residual alpha. Realized funding is assessed about the same as that curve, so cash at the zero official-SOFR benchmark is not under-earning a secret carry edge, and shocked-risk capital would only mean paying SOFR for a priced view. Stay flat.
no-trade-skeptic.invalidation: Actionable only if a later frozen packet shows realized SOFR printing away from the strip by enough to beat paying SOFR on shocked-risk capital, plus a dated catalyst and a falsifiable entry that survives crowding and overnight-horizon checks.
